critique: The matched minimax conclusions cover two project-defined polynomial regimes: an isolated class with a specific upper packing envelope and a pervasive class with order-h^{-1} thin-site multiplicity; they do not characterize the frontier for general thickness profiles. The arbitrary-modulus result is only a two-sided bracket because its global-entropy upper bound can remain logarithmically larger than the lower-profile converse. The band theorem establishes global rate-optimal width on the base and pervasive classes, but neither local-oracle width achievability over arbitrary triangular unions nor the proposed score-law distinguishability characterization is proved. The framing leaves those items open, so the delivered field-level contribution is the two-regime separation, count-adaptive pervasive estimator, and pervasive global band-width frontier rather than a general adaptive frontier.
